description.narrative:
Sensitise Uganda proposes to implement project called “Youth civic participation in secondary schools”. The goal of the project is to promote civic engagement and support democratic and participatory good governance for the students to become more responsible andactive citizens as they grow up. Specifically the project seeks to;- i. To empower students with the political and civic knowledge and capacity to stand as electoral candidates, speech writers, and election observers. ii. To Provide students the platform to engage in active citizenship through providing the technicalities and issues involved in democratic governance. iii. To enhance the students’ knowledge and ability to analyze, evaluate, take and defend positions on public issues, and to use their knowledge to participate in civic and political processes. Civic education will expose students to the nation’s values and constitution, their rights, duties and obligations and how good citizens of a country should be ready to perform their civic responsibilities towards the growth and development of their society and the nation at large.
This project will be implemented in Wakiso district targeting 3 secondary schools that is; one girls’ school and two mixed schools (with both girls and boys) to ensure gender equality. Students with disabilities will be highly encouraged to participate in the project activities to ensure disability inclusion and mainstreaming and no student will be discriminated on basis of gender, sexual orientation, disability among others.
500 students will have participated in civic engagement activities during the project life cycle. The project will enhance the capacity of the girls and students with disabilities to express their views themselves, build their confidence and take up leadership roles. By the end of the project, there will be increased civic knowledge, civic skills and civic disposition. That is;- students will have understood the workings of the political system and of their own political and civic rights and responsibilities. The students’ ability to analyze, evaluate, take and defend positions on public issues, and to use their knowledge to participate in civic and political processes will have increased. Students’ traits necessary for a democracy will have been built.
These will be achieved through the following activities; a mapping exercise to identify key partners to work with, a project inception meeting, school-based meetings with the school leadership to introduce the project, develop a civic education handbook, launch the civic education handbook, produce a wide range of Civic educationIEC materials, conduct school debate competitions on key public issues, policies and laws, Conduct annual article writing competitions on key public issues, organize and support school guild elections, support students to participate in international day celebrations like International Youth Day, conduct annual sharing and reflection platforms between students, support students to attend the Parliament week, organise and conduct a leadership Camp for the elected student guild leaders, conduct mentorship for students, carryout project monitoring with partners, conduct end of project video documentary, support staff to participate in voice Linking and Learning events.

participating-org.narrative:
Sensitise Uganda with our slogan #illuminating Ugandans for development and positive transformation# is an indigenous/local, national Non Governmental Organization (NGO) whose tremendous aim was to sensitise, build capacity, raise awareness, implement projects and programs to all Ugandans aimed at enhancing socio-economic and political development of individuals, communities and the country as a whole.
Sensitise Uganda was founded on the 15th day of February-2013 but was formally registered on 14th February 2014 with theGovernment of the Republic of Uganda (Ministry of Internal Affairs-NGO board) under the Non-Governmental Organizations RegistrationAct, Cap. 113 with registration Number 10407. Sensitise Uganda was re-registered on 7th September 2019under the Non-Governmental Organizations Act 2016 and was issued a registration certificate with Registration Number INDR107872891NB and also issued an operationlicense Number INDP104072891NB under file Number MIA/NB/2013/11/2891.
The day to day activities of Sensitise Uganda are run by thesecretariat which is headed by the Executive Director and supervised by the Board of Directors of Sensitise Uganda. Sensitise Uganda headquarters apparently are located at Plot 106 Nsubuga Road, Off Kisaasi-KyanjaRoad, Nakawa Division, Kampala City in Uganda. Allthe members of Sensitise Uganda are non-partisan. Sensitise Uganda is a youth led and youth focused and covers the whole of Uganda.
With partners we have been able to achieve a number of things to improve the lives of men, women, girls and boys suffering from poverty, injustice, insecurity and exclusion. We were able to consult young people in Uganda and we developed the National Youth Manifesto 2016-2021: The National Youth Manifesto is a set of policydemands by young Ugandans calling on government and candidates to make the best possible contributions to the development of the country. It sets priority demands that call on government to harness thepotential of the youth to benefit from available opportunities. It provides an opportunity to the country to adopt a youth-led approach to development to achieve the national vision #A transformed Ugandan society from a peasant to a modern and prosperous country within 30 years. The manifesto is hinged offive key thematic areas of employment, health, education, youth participation in decisionmaking and sports and creative arts. Through advocacy while using the national youth manifesto, a lot has been achieved though moreis needed. Unemployment has somehow reduced due to introduction of skills training, the health of Uganda people has improve, the education curriculum has been revised to address the mismatch between the jobs available and the skills acquired.
We have contributedto the review of different laws; Case in point in the Kampala Capital City Authority (KCCA Act), the law that governs the capital city of Uganda Kampala. Formerly it was not recognising youth structures and therefore youth structures could not benefit meaningfully from theKCCAservices, through our advocacy the law was amended and now among other good amendments, youth are recognised within the KCCA Act 2019 as amended.
We facilitated and contributed to the review of the Disability Amendment Bill where we hired a consultantto analyse the law to find the missing links which were presented to parliament with consultations from the Disabled People#s Organisations (DPOs). We are currently involved in the review of the Sexual Offences Bill 2019 which is before the parliamentofthe republic of Uganda.
We were able to train over 300 youth leaders in the national Youth Council in the districts of Kampala, Hoima, Kasese, Ntungamo, Isingiro, Kabale among others to understand their leadership roles and how they can be able to influence government policies and positions to be pro-youth.
We have been able on an annual basis to influence the national budget process to make sure theissues of the marginalised especial youth and women are well captured and financed.
We arecurrentlyamong other activities and efforts implementing the national youth manifesto to be incorporated into the local government planning processes so that all issues of youth in the manifesto are financed and implemented.
The Vision: An informed, coherent, sensitized, transformed and a developed Uganda.
Mission Statement: To sensitise, raise awareness, build capacity of Ugandans on socio-economic and political challenges through implementing projects and programs.

comment.narrative: While Sensitise Uganda had planned for 2 alliances, coalitions, and networks, 7 were established and successfully initiated activities based on joint action plans, leading to significant outcomes. These results were achieved by leveraging the collective expertise and resources of the networks, facilitating effective communication, and mobilizing support for rightsholder groups. The partnerships also ensured coordinated advocacy efforts and streamlined implementation of the civic education handbook, empowering rightsholders with practical skills for active participation.

comment.narrative: Several videos were been produced and a publication of the civic education handbook amplifying the issues faced by grantees and rightsholders. These publications have effectively raised awareness, influenced stakeholder engagement, and facilitated discussions around the needs of youth in civic participation. The results were achieved through collaborative efforts between the rightsholders, other partners like the Uganda Human Rights Commission and the project team, fostering a shared commitment to highlighting youth voices in decision-making processes and generating visibility for the grantees' change agendas.

description.narrative: % rightsholder groups indicating increased confidence to raise their voice

comment.narrative: 137 rightsholders demonstrated increased confidence in advocating for their rights and participating in civic activities. This growth in confidence was achieved through a combination of leadership training and platforms for dialogue such as debate competitions and reflection meetings. These interventions equipped the youth with the necessary skills and knowledge to articulate their concerns effectively. Additionally, ongoing mentorship, support from school administrations, and the use of civic education handbooks empowered them to engage meaningfully in school governance and other civic matters.
